Pentobarbital and Omeprazole Interaction: Pentobarbital reduces the levels or effects of omeprazole by altering the metabolism of the hepatic enzyme CYP2C19. Close monitoring is required when these drugs are co-administered. 2. Omeprazole and Pexidartinib Interaction: Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Avoid co-administration of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) with pexidartinib. If necessary, use H2-receptor antagonists or antacids instead. When using alternatives, administer pexidartinib two hours before or after locally-acting antacids, or at least two hours before or ten hours after H2-receptor antagonists. 3. Phenobarbital and Omeprazole Interaction: Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting the metabolism of hepatic enzymes CYP2C19 and CYP3A4. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Close monitoring is advised. 4. Phenytoin and Omeprazole Interaction: Phenytoin reduces the levels or effects of omeprazole by altering the metabolism of hepatic enzymes CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Omeprazole and Phytoestrogens Interaction: Omeprazole decreases phytoestrogen levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 6. Omeprazole and Polysaccharide Iron Interaction: Omeprazole reduces the levels or effects of polysaccharide iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Omeprazole and Ponatinib Interaction: Omeprazole decreases ponatinib levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 8. Omeprazole and Posaconazole Interaction: Omeprazole reduces the levels or effects of posaconazole by increasing gastric pH. Posaconazole, in turn, increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting the metabolism of hepatic enzymes CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Primidone and Omeprazole Interaction: Primidone decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by altering the metabolism of hepatic enzymes CYP2C19 and CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Omeprazole and Quazepam Interaction: Omeprazole increases quazepam levels by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 11. Ribociclib and Omeprazole Interaction: Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting the metabolism of hepatic enzymes CYP3A4. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 12. Rifampin and Omeprazole Interaction: Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by altering the metabolism of hepatic enzymes CYP2C19 and CYP3A4. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Close monitoring is required. 13. Rifapentine and Omeprazole Interaction: Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting the metabolism of hepatic enzymes CYP3A4. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 14. Omeprazole and Rilpivirine Interaction: Omeprazole decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Concurrent use is contraindicated as it may lead to treatment failure or resistance to rilpivirine or NNRTIs. 15. Omeprazole and Riociguat Interaction: Omeprazole reduces the levels or effects of riociguat by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Ritonavir and Omeprazole Interaction: Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by altering the metabolism of hepatic enzymes CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Omeprazole and Rose Hips Interaction: Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Omeprazole and Ruxolitinib Interaction: Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by affecting the metabolism of hepatic enzymes CYP3A4. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 19. Omeprazole and Sotrasib Interaction: Omeprazole decreases sotrasib levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, administer sotrasib four hours before or ten hours after locally-acting antacids. 20. St. John’s Wort and Omeprazole Interaction: St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by altering the metabolism of hepatic enzymes CYP2C19. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Stiripentol and Omeprazole Interaction: Stiripentol increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting the metabolism of hepatic enzymes CYP2C19. Consider reducing the dose of CYP2C19 substrates if adverse reactions occur. Monitor closely. 22. Omeprazole and Tacrolimus Interaction: Omeprazole increases tacrolimus levels by altering the metabolism of hepatic enzymes CYP2C19. Concomitant administration may increase tacrolimus concentrations, particularly in intermediate or poor metabolizers of CYP2C19. Monitor closely. 23. Tazemetostat and Omeprazole Interaction: Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting the metabolism of hepatic enzymes CYP3A4. Omeprazole increases tazemetostat levels by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Omeprazole and Theophylline Interaction: Omeprazole increases the toxicity of theophylline due to prolonged use of PPIs, which can cause hypochlorhydria. Monitor for toxicity. 25. Omeprazole and Thyroid Desiccated Interaction: Omeprazole decreases thyroid desiccated levels by increasing gastric pH. Conflicting evidence exists regarding this interaction. Monitor closely. 26. Omeprazole and Tinidazole Interaction: Omeprazole increases tinidazole levels by affecting the metabolism of hepatic enzymes CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Omeprazole and Tofacitinib Interaction: Omeprazole increases tofacitinib levels by altering the metabolism of hepatic enzymes CYP2C19. No specific dose adjustment is recommended unless co-administered with both moderate CYP3A4 and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors. 28. Omeprazole and Triazolam Interaction: Omeprazole increases triazolam levels by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 29. Triclabendazole and Omeprazole Interaction: Triclabendazole increases omeprazole levels by affecting the metabolism of hepatic enzymes CYP2C19. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Tucatinib and Omeprazole Interaction: Tucatinib increases omeprazole levels by affecting the metabolism of hepatic enzymes CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose as per product labeling. 31. Omeprazole and Vismodegib Interaction: Omeprazole decreases vismodegib levels by altering its solubility due to increased gastric pH. The effect on efficacy is unknown. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Voriconazole and Omeprazole Interaction: Voriconazole increases omeprazole levels by affecting the metabolism of hepatic enzymes CYP2C19 and CYP3A4. Omeprazole also increases voriconazole levels by the same mechanism. Monitor closely. 33. Omeprazole and Warfarin Interaction: Omeprazole increases warfarin levels by affecting the metabolism of its R-enantiomer via CYP3A4. Monitor INR more frequently and adjust the warfarin dose if needed. 34. Severe Adverse Reactions: Omeprazole and its components have been associated with severe cutaneous adverse reactions (e.g., Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, DRESS). Discontinue therapy at the first signs of these reactions. 35. Clostridioides difficile-Associated Diarrhea (CDAD): PPIs, including omeprazole, have been linked to CDAD, which can range from mild diarrhea to fatal colitis. Assess all patients presenting with diarrhea after therapy initiation and discontinue if confirmed. 36. Hormonal Contraceptive Efficacy: Omeprazole may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Patients should use an additional non-hormonal contraceptive method during therapy. 37. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Omeprazole may cause fetal harm based on animal studies. It is generally not recommended during pregnancy. Breastfeeding considerations should weigh the benefits of therapy against potential risks to the infant. 38. Administration Instructions: Omeprazole capsules should be swallowed whole with a full glass of water and not crushed or chewed. Avoid alcohol during therapy.
